newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks shade back gains at close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks shade back gains at close.

text.p: French shares finished firm and above resistance on the CAC-40 index on Tuesday but just off the day's high.

Traders said the unfolding saga of a reported bid by investment group CGIP for the Cerus holding company and Valeo, the car parts maker, had the market spellbound. They view Cerus as being in play and want more information on the "options" being explored in talks between CGIP and cash-strapped Italian magnate Carlo De Benedetti.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 21.82 points or 1.08 percent at 2,042.12. Chartists said the 2,031-35 area marked major resistance.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up 23 points at 2,047 from Monday's close.
Volume was a solid 6.01 billion francs
Cerus ended 2.80 francs lower at 133, or 2.06 percent, after CGIP denied it was planning a public offer for Cerus and Valeo, in which Cerus holds 28 percent.
However, CGIP said it was in talks with De Benedetti over other options but gave no further details. Cerus and Valeo were both suspended limit-down in the morning .
CGIP closed up 34 francs at 1,189, or 2.94 percent, while Valeo was up 9.10 francs at 279.60

Car-maker Renault posted after the close a first half net attributable profit of 158 million francs and forecast only a slight improvement in the cars unit in the second half. The stock closed up 1.90 francs at 119.
Broker recommendations, including Paris brokerage Dupont Denant and U.S. house JP Morgan, boosted oil major Elf Aquitaine which closed up 4.50 francs at 393.
